title: Dino Tour
intro: Travel back in time through the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous to meet the dinosaurs!
milestones: You reached the giant fern forest!
You found a field of fossil footprints!
You made it past the bubbling volcano!
You reached the big blue lake!
You climbed over the rocky ridge!
You found a hidden dinosaur nest!
You crossed the wide river delta!
You reached the tall conifer woods!
You can see your destination ahead!
detours: Oh no, a volcano is rumbling! Solve {count} problems to find a safe path around it.
A herd of long-necked dinosaurs is crossing the trail. Solve {count} problems while you wait for them to pass!
Your time machine needs a quick repair. Solve {count} problems to fix it!
A river flooded the path! Solve {count} problems to build a log bridge.
Thick fog rolled in. Solve {count} problems to find the trail again!
Sticky mud is everywhere! Solve {count} problems to pull your boots free.
A big rock slid onto the path. Solve {count} problems to roll it away!
A curious little dinosaur took your map! Solve {count} problems to get it back.
detourCleared: You did it! Back on the trail.
Great work! The path is clear again.
setback: Uh-oh, that detour was tricky! Let's go back to the last flag and try again. You can do it!
No problem! Explorers sometimes take the long way. Back to the last flag we go!

eoraptor: Eoraptor is one of the earliest dinosaurs ever found.
It lived about 231 million years ago in what is now Argentina.
It probably ate both plants and animals.
herrerasaurus: Herrerasaurus was one of the first big meat-eating dinosaurs.
It lived about 231 million years ago in Argentina.
coelophysis: Coelophysis was about 9 feet long but weighed only about 30 pounds.
Hundreds of them were found together at Ghost Ranch in New Mexico.
It had the first wishbone ever found in a dinosaur fossil.
plateosaurus: Plateosaurus was a plant-eater that lived in Europe.
Scientists have found 33 Plateosaurus skeletons, more than almost any other Triassic dinosaur.
staurikosaurus: Staurikosaurus is one of the oldest dinosaurs ever found, about 233 million years old.
It was a meat-eater from Brazil.
Only 2 Staurikosaurus skeletons have been found.
nyasasaurus: Nyasasaurus lived more than 240 million years ago in Tanzania, in Africa.
It might be the oldest dinosaur of all!
Scientists are still deciding whether it is a true dinosaur or a very close cousin.
eodromaeus: Eodromaeus was a small meat-eater from Argentina.
It lived at the same time and in the same place as Eoraptor.
Scientists call it a dinosaur from the dawn of the dinosaur age.
saturnalia: Saturnalia was an early cousin of the giant long-necked dinosaurs.
It ate plants and lived in Brazil.
Only 3 Saturnalia skeletons have been found.
buriolestes: Buriolestes was an early cousin of the giant long-necked plant-eaters.
It shows that the long-necked dinosaur family started out as hunters.
panphagia: It ate both plants and animals.
Only one Panphagia skeleton has ever been found, in Argentina.
pisanosaurus: Pisanosaurus was a small plant-eater from Argentina.
Only one Pisanosaurus skeleton has ever been found.
Scientists still argue about which dinosaur family it belongs to.
liliensternus: Liliensternus was one of the biggest meat-eaters of the Triassic.
Its fossils were found in Germany and Switzerland.
It laid eggs, and 5 Liliensternus skeletons are known.
tawa: Tawa was a meat-eater that lived in New Mexico.
Scientists found a complete Tawa skeleton.
It helps scientists understand how the early meat-eating dinosaurs developed.
chindesaurus: Chindesaurus was a meat-eater that lived more than 200 million years ago.
The first Chindesaurus fossil was found in Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona.
daemonosaurus: Daemonosaurus had a short snout and big buck teeth!
It was a meat-eater from Ghost Ranch in New Mexico.
Scientists have found only its skull.
riojasaurus: Riojasaurus was a large, heavy plant-eater.
Only 2 Riojasaurus skeletons have been found.
melanorosaurus: Melanorosaurus was a heavy plant-eater that walked on four legs.
About 10 Melanorosaurus skeletons have been found.
thecodontosaurus: Thecodontosaurus was found in England in 1834.
That was 8 years before the word "dinosaur" was even invented!
It was only the fourth dinosaur ever given a name.
efraasia: Efraasia was a plant-eater from Germany.
It was an early relative of Plateosaurus.
ingentia: Ingentia was a giant, about 26 to 33 feet long!
It lived in Argentina, long before the biggest long-necked dinosaurs.
It shows that dinosaurs grew huge earlier than scientists once thought.
stegosaurus: Stegosaurus had big plates on its back and spikes on its tail.
It lived in the western United States and in Portugal.
brachiosaurus: Brachiosaurus was a giant long-necked dinosaur shaped a bit like a giraffe.
It weighed about 29,000 kilograms. That's around 64,000 pounds!
Being so huge helped keep it safe from predators.
allosaurus: Allosaurus was the top predator of the Late Jurassic.
The biggest Allosaurus found was about 32 feet long.
diplodocus: Diplodocus had a very long, whip-like tail.
Its name means "double beam," after the bones under its tail.
Tracks and skeletons show it stood up tall, not sprawled on its belly.
apatosaurus-brontosaurus: For many years, people used the name Brontosaurus for Apatosaurus.
In 2015, scientists decided Brontosaurus is its own kind of dinosaur after all!
Apatosaurus weighed about 19,500 kilograms. That's around 43,000 pounds!
archaeopteryx: Archaeopteryx was a feathered dinosaur that could fly.
It weighed only about half a pound.
It is one of the most famous links between dinosaurs and birds.
dilophosaurus: Dilophosaurus had two flat crests on its head.
The crests were probably for showing off, not for fighting.
It was about 6 meters long. That's nearly 20 feet!
ceratosaurus: Ceratosaurus had a horn on its nose.
It was a meat-eater that lived in Utah, Colorado and Tanzania.
It weighed about 670 kilograms, around 1,500 pounds.
camarasaurus: Camarasaurus is the most common long-necked dinosaur found in North America.
Its name means "chambered lizard," after the hollow spaces in its backbone.
Each of its feet had a hooked claw on the inside toe.
megalosaurus: Megalosaurus was the first dinosaur ever given a name, in 1824.
People were digging up its bones long before anyone knew what a dinosaur was.
giraffatitan: Giraffatitan was a giant long-necked plant-eater from Tanzania, in Africa.
It looks a lot like its American cousin, Brachiosaurus.
It was dug up at a famous fossil site called Tendaguru.
compsognathus: Compsognathus was about the size of a chicken.
It weighed only about 2.5 kilograms, around 5½ pounds.
It was a meat-eater from Germany and France.
kentrosaurus: Kentrosaurus was a spiky stegosaur from Tanzania, in Africa.
It weighed about 321 kilograms, around 700 pounds.
torvosaurus: Torvosaurus was one of the biggest meat-eaters of the Jurassic.
Its fossils have been found in Colorado and in Portugal.
mamenchisaurus: Mamenchisaurus had an extremely long neck, up to about half the length of its body!
It was a plant-eater, and 24 Mamenchisaurus skeletons are known.
guanlong: Guanlong was an early relative of Tyrannosaurus rex.
It had a crest on its head.
cryolophosaurus: It had an unusual crest that ran sideways across its head.
Only one Cryolophosaurus skeleton has ever been found.
scelidosaurus: Scelidosaurus was one of the earliest armored dinosaurs.
It was found in Dorset, England.
massospondylus: Scientists have found Massospondylus eggs with babies still inside!
It was a plant-eater from southern Africa.
heterodontosaurus: Heterodontosaurus had three different kinds of teeth, including tusks!
It was tiny, weighing only about 1.8 kilograms, around 4 pounds.
tyrannosaurus-rex: Tyrannosaurus rex is the most famous meat-eating dinosaur.
The biggest complete T. rex skeleton is 40 feet long.
Skin fossils show that grown-up T. rex were mostly covered in scales.
triceratops: Triceratops had three horns and a big frill on its head.
It lived at the very end of the age of dinosaurs.
velociraptor: Velociraptor had feathers and was about the size of a turkey.
It had a curved, sickle-shaped claw on each foot.
Real Velociraptors were much smaller than the ones in movies.
spinosaurus: Spinosaurus had a tall sail on its back.
Scientists still debate how much time it spent in the water.
ankylosaurus: It had a heavy club at the end of its tail.
It was a plant-eater that lived in North America.
iguanodon: Iguanodon had a sharp spike on each thumb.
It was the second dinosaur ever named, in 1825.
Dozens of Iguanodon skeletons were found together in a coal mine in Belgium.
parasaurolophus: Parasaurolophus had a long, tube-shaped crest on its head.
It probably used its crest to make sounds.
This duck-billed dinosaur weighed about 2,500 kilograms.
pachycephalosaurus: Pachycephalosaurus had a thick, dome-shaped head.
Some scientists think Dracorex and Stygimoloch were really young Pachycephalosaurus.
It was a plant-eater from the western United States.
giganotosaurus: Giganotosaurus was about 40 feet long, roughly as big as T. rex!
Only 3 Giganotosaurus skeletons have been found.
argentinosaurus: Argentinosaurus was one of the biggest land animals ever.
It may have been about 100 feet long!
Only one skeleton has been found, discovered in 1987.
carnotaurus: It had two thick horns above its eyes and tiny arms.
It was about 25 feet long and lived in Argentina.
deinonychus: Deinonychus was a raptor that weighed about 75 kilograms, around 165 pounds.
Its discovery changed the way scientists think about dinosaurs.
utahraptor: Utahraptor is the biggest raptor ever found, about 20 feet long.
It was the top predator where it lived.
therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurus had giant claws, up to about 3 feet long!
It ate plants, even though its relatives ate meat.
edmontosaurus: Edmontosaurus was a duck-billed dinosaur with a face like a shovel.
Some Edmontosaurus fossils are "mummies" that still show the shape of its skin.
protoceratops: Protoceratops was about the size of a sheep.
One famous fossil shows a Protoceratops fighting a Velociraptor!
It lived in the Gobi Desert.
oviraptor: But it was really guarding its own nest!
microraptor: Microraptor had feathered wings on both its arms and its legs.
It could glide through the air.
carcharodontosaurus: Its teeth looked like the teeth of a great white shark.
The first fossils ever found were destroyed during World War II.
baryonyx: It had a head like a crocodile's and caught fish.
